note: Rewritten from Hill's (1922) original description, original in English; that work placed the species in the genus Hamitermes, later assigned to Amitermes. The text is taken from the OCR of the BHL fascicle scan held by Zenodo (record 2333936); the original uses a raised dot as the decimal point, which the OCR renders either as a hyphen or as "•", restored here to the decimal point according to the context.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head and base of the mandibles orange, the apex of the mandibles rusty; antennae iron-yellow, darker than the head; the rest pale straw. Head including the mandibles (fig. 22) twice as long as wide, the posterior margin and sides rounded. Mandibles very long, sickle-shaped, with a sharp hooked tooth before the middle. Labrum nearly as long as wide, anterior margin rounded. Clypeus large and wide, with a shallow median depression, not reaching the posterior margin. Antennae 15-segmented, long and slender; segment 1 long and narrow, twice as long as segment 2; segment 2 cylindrical; segment 3 short and narrow, the shortest and smallest of all; segments 4 and 5 similar, about twice as long as segment 3; segment 6 longer, nearly as long as segment 7; segments 7—12 similar; segments 13 and 14 slightly longer; segment 15 longer than segment 14, bluntly pointed at the end. Pronotum shaped as in A. perplexus, with scattered long red hairs. Legs moderately slender, similar to those of the foregoing, the lower side of the fore tibia with a row of long stout hairs on the distal half. Abdomen wide at the middle, narrowing towards the pointed end. Cerci short. Measurements: body length 5.5 mm; head length including mandibles 2.16 mm; head width 1.17 mm; mandible length 1 mm; antennal length 2.03 mm; thorax and abdomen length 3.5 mm; pronotum length 0.42 mm, width 0.7 mm; tibia length (fore/mid/hind) 0.92/0.84/1.17 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head and thorax pale straw; antennae much darker towards the apex; the rest nearly white, clothed with red hairs. Posterior margin of the head rounded, the sides straighter than usual. Labrum large, narrower at the base than at the middle. Anteclypeus large, projecting forwards. Postclypeus large, convex, anterior margin truncate, posterior margin rounded. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 1 twice as long as segment 2; segment 3 very short and narrow, the smallest; segments 4 and 5 about equal in length; segment 6 larger; segments 7—15 increasing in length. Pronotum rounded and upturned anteriorly, anterolateral corners rounded, posterior margin rounded and slightly concave, with red hairs of unequal length. Legs rather short and slender. Abdomen elongate-oval, clothed with red hairs. Basal half of the cerci short and wide, the remaining two-thirds slender. Measurements: body length 5.25 mm; head length including mandibles 1.5 mm; head width 1.12 mm; antennal length 1.41 mm; thorax and abdomen length 3.76 mm; pronotum length 0.37 mm, width 0.84 mm; tibia length (fore/mid/hind) 0.86/0.7/1 mm; abdominal width 1.8 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Most closely related to A. germanus of the Northern Territory, differing in the much larger size, the larger and rounder labrum, and the larger clypeus of different shape; the antennal segmentation of the two is similar, and the mandibles similar apart from size. The type series is 1 soldier with numerous nymphs and workers (in alcohol) and 9 soldiers and 9 workers (on cards), deposited in the South Australian Museum, the paratypes with the author. Distribution: Mount Lofty Ranges, Gawler and Angaston, South Australia.
